A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same embodied image-captioning work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gibson and HM3D experiments, captioning comparisons, triplet-weight and ground-truth-detection ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional LLM-choice experiments, inference timings, and occlusion-test results.

M1.justification: The CLA exploration policy, voxel-based object grouping, frequency-and-example-based LD-CPS prompting, and captioning-plus-triplet training remain unchanged. The additional LLM configurations are ablation variants within the retained pipeline.

E1.justification: Gibson, HM3D, and the indoor-object captioning task remain. v2 Appendix VI adds a targeted test scenario comprising 50 manually collected images under varying occlusion, extending evaluation of challenging input conditions within the existing domains.

E2.justification: v2 Table IV adds component-level comparisons using Mistral-7B and Qwen3-8B within LD-CPS, compared with the existing LLaMa configuration. The ECO, IC3, exploration-policy, and captioner comparators in the main experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The main splits, training budgets, exploration length, and metrics remain unchanged. v2 introduces alternative LLM configurations, a 50-image occlusion protocol pooling Gibson and HM3D results, and timing measurements over specified steps, boxes, and objects. It removes the ground-truth-object control using 25 training and five validation scenes. The new occlusion test's stated per-category counts do not reconcile with the six classes listed in Section IV-B.

E4.justification: The supplementary validation substantially changes its diagnostic scope: v2 adds LLM-choice sensitivity and quantitative and qualitative occlusion-robustness tests, while removing v1's ground-truth-object-detection ablation and HM3D exploration-disagreement analysis. The triplet-weight ablation and existing qualitative caption comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new timing averages specify measurement sample counts but introduce no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables I–II and the triplet-weight results in v1 Table IV/v2 Table V match numerically. v2 adds LLM-choice scores, timings, and occlusion results; its new occlusion test reports CoCa cosine similarity of 68.71 without fine-tuning and 74.03 with triplet fine-tuning. The ground-truth-detection results and HM3D exploration distribution are removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the state and loss definitions, and the assumption that inaccurate captions are not the majority retain the same mathematical substance. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the modular self-supervised framework, frequency-based pseudo-captioning, and improved caption accuracy and consistency. The additional experiments do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains CLA's high-similarity observations through initial map building, elaborates frequency- and pose-related failure mechanisms, and explicitly states that the framework is not optimized for real-time operation on a standalone robot. It adds interpretations of LLM sensitivity and occlusion robustness while removing the segmentation-control interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies an NVIDIA Tesla V100 16GB and provides component timings and measurement counts, plus the new LLM variant names and sizes. Existing hyperparameters, augmentation, deduplication, planning details, prompts, and access information are retained, partly in Appendix I. The shortened bounding-box filtering description loses the explicit reference to overlap with Mask2Former boxes.

R1.justification: v2 adds the two Bigazzi embodied-exploration works, Tan's Embodied Scene Description, and Active Neural SLAM. It distinguishes object-view consistency from diverse scene descriptions and clarifies the exploration policy's research lineage.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits and moves dataset descriptions, planning, deduplication, and augmentation details into an expanded Appendix I. It reorganizes the supplementary sections, labels the limitations paragraph, and adds acknowledgements while preserving the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the LLM-choice table, occlusion table, and occlusion figure, and removes v1's ground-truth-detection table and HM3D exploration figure. Retained figure artwork is unchanged; tables and prompt listings are repositioned or renumbered within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful LLM sensitivity, occlusion evidence, hardware-specific timings, and a deployment limitation. However, it removes segmentation-control and HM3D-policy evidence and overstates the new LLM comparison: CoCa/Mistral trails ECO on all six metrics, including SPICE 29.29 versus 33.34, despite claiming superiority across LLM choices (Tables IV and I). With the main evidence unchanged, these benefits and losses leave the net quality direction unclear.
